item.title: OH SCR14: Urge Congress to reject moratorium on state regulation of AI

bill.title: Urge Congress to reject moratorium on state regulation of AI
bill.description: To urge the Congress of the United States to reject any moratorium on state laws regulating artificial intelligence.

136th General Assembly

Senator Blessing
A C O N C U R R E N T R E S O L U T I O N
To urge the Congress of the United States to reject any 1
moratorium on state laws regulating artificial 2
intelligence. 3
BE IT RESOLVED BY THE SENATE OF THE STATE OF OHIO (THE HOUSE OF
REPRESENTATIVES CONCURRING):
WHEREAS, The United States Congress rejected an effort to 4
insert a moratorium on artificial intelligence regulation in the 5
National Defense Authorization Act; and 6
WHEREAS, A similar moratorium was stricken by the Senate 7
from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act; and 8
WHEREAS, The Tenth Amendment of the United States 9
Constitution provides that powers not explicitly delegated to 10
the federal government remain with the states; and 11
WHEREAS, The power to regulate artificial intelligence is 12
not explicitly delegated to the federal government; and 13
WHEREAS, The states, as the laboratories of democracy, are 14
best positioned to respond quickly to emerging harms and tailor 15
policy to local needs; and 16
WHEREAS, Congress currently has no plan to regulate 17
artificial intelligence on a federal level; and 18
WHEREAS, Large artificial intelligence companies and their 19

trade associations support and have lobbied for a moratorium on 20
state laws regulating artificial intelligence; and 21
WHEREAS, A moratorium on state laws regulating artificial 22
intelligence places profits over the health, safety, and welfare 23
of Americans; and 24
WHEREAS, Executive orders attempting to legislate 25
artificial intelligence policy are blatantly unconstitutional; 26
now therefore be it 27
RESOLVED, That we, the members of the 136th General 28
Assembly of the State of Ohio, condemn the idea of an artificial 29
intelligence legislation moratorium in all of its iterations and 30
urge members of Congress to reject inclusion of such language as 31
part of any federal legislation and executive orders; and be it 32
further 33
RESOLVED, That the Clerk of the Senate transmit duly 34
authenticated copies of this resolution to the President Pro 35
Tempore and Secretary of the United States Senate and the 36
Speaker and Clerk of the United States House of Representatives. 37
